long_biography.plain_text:
David Boies built his professional reputation around courtroom advocacy and a preference for turning complex disputes into clear narratives. After thirty years at Cravath, he left in 1997 and co-founded Boies Schiller Flexner with Jonathan Schiller. The new practice grew from a three-lawyer boutique into a national litigation firm, while Boies served as chairman through 2024.

His legal formation combined antitrust study at Yale with later teaching at New York University and Cardozo. He has described trust as a lawyer's most important professional asset and narrative as central to trial work. Outside the firm, he helped establish Hawk and Horse Vineyards on a California ranch, a family-run agricultural business managed separately from his legal practice.
